missing_details: The sentence is truncated: the paper states that the maximum is taken over p′-subgroups H of G.
The conjecture should explicitly quantify over a prime p and a finite group G.
To make the question stand-alone, k(H) should be defined as the number of conjugacy classes of H.
To make the left-hand side fully explicit, one may write it as |IBr_p(G)|, where IBr_p(G) is the set of irreducible p-Brauer characters of G.
To make the subgroup condition fully explicit, a p′-subgroup should be identified as a subgroup H <= G with p not dividing |H|.

No extra hypotheses such as solvable, p-solvable, quasi-simple, blockwise, or nilpotent should be added: the paper’s problem is stated for arbitrary finite groups. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
refined_question: Let p be a prime and G a finite group. Is it always true that |IBr_p(G)| <= max{ k(H) : H <= G and p does not divide |H| }, where IBr_p(G) denotes the set of irreducible p-Brauer characters of G and k(H) denotes the number of conjugacy classes of H?
